hero.headline: Indian River County public schools to close Friday as flooding shuts roads
hero.teaser: Public schools across Indian River County will be closed Friday, Nov. 20, after flooding left more roads impassable and raised concerns about additional rain. The School District o
hero.body:
Public schools across Indian River County will be closed Friday, Nov. 20, after flooding left more roads impassable and raised concerns about additional rain. The School District of Indian River County announced the decision Thursday, pointing to localized flooding, already saturated ground and the potential for more heavy rainfall. District officials said the shutdown was intended to protect students, their families and school employees.

 The announcement applies to all of the county’s public schools. It comes as road closures increase, particularly in Vero Lake Estates, and water levels rise at the district’s North County Transportation compound.

 The county’s road closure map showed nine road closures and four lane closures Thursday. Among the roads listed as closed were 100th Court, 103rd Avenue, 104th Avenue, 83rd Street and 87th Street. Those five roads were part of the larger set of closures shown on the map, rather than a complete list of affected roads.

 Vero Lake Estates was a particular concern in both the district’s closure announcement and the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office’s flooding reports. The district cited the growing number of road closures there, while the sheriff’s office reported additional flooded roads in the neighborhood.

 Deputies warned motorists against driving into standing water. Floodwater can be deeper than it looks, and vehicles can stall after entering it, according to the sheriff’s office. That warning accompanied the agency’s reports of more flooded roads in Vero Lake Estates.

 High-water vehicles are in the area, and anyone who becomes stranded should call 911. The safety message applies even when a driver cannot judge the depth of water covering a road: its appearance may not reflect how deep it actually is. The sheriff’s office’s advice was to stay out of the water rather than attempt to drive through it.

 A flood watch remains in effect for Indian River County through Friday evening, with additional showers and thunderstorms possible. The National Weather Service reported that parts of eastern Indian River County had received 2 to 4 inches of rain. The possibility of further rainfall, combined with saturated ground and existing flooding, was among the reasons the district gave for canceling Friday’s classes.

 Beyond the weather-related closure, schools will also be closed for Thanksgiving break. The district’s immediate concern Thursday was the flooding affecting local roads and its North County Transportation compound, with Friday’s shutdown intended to keep students, families and employees safe.

cards.headline: Flooded roads disrupt Indian River County travel; trash service could be affected
cards.teaser: Officials urged drivers to avoid flooded roads in Vero Lake Estates and watch two potential trouble spots in Fellsmere. Unsafe conditions could also disrupt trash collection and close waste facilities early.
cards.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff’s Office reported more flooded roads in Vero Lake Estates on Thursday as heavy rain moved through the county, while county officials warned that unsafe conditions could disrupt trash collection and waste facilities. The sheriff’s office urged drivers to stay off flooded roads because water can be deeper than it appears and can stall vehicles. High-water vehicles are in the area, and anyone who becomes stranded should call 911.

 The county’s road closure map listed nine road closures and four lane closures as of 10:53 a.m. Thursday. Roads marked closed included 100th Court, 103rd Avenue, 104th Avenue, 83rd Street and 87th Street.

 Lane-closure listings included 101st Avenue and West 98th Avenue. In Fellsmere, the city urged drivers to use extreme caution and identified New York Avenue near Hickory Street and North Broadway as potential trouble spots. Those roads could close if rain continues, the city said. City Hall remains open and operating normally.

 The county warned that heavy rain and gusty winds could disrupt trash collection. Residents whose streets are flooded were asked not to put their carts in the water. The landfill and customer convenience centers could close early if conditions become unsafe.

 A flood watch remains in effect for Indian River County through Friday evening, with more showers and thunderstorms possible. The National Weather Service issued a flood advisory Thursday morning for eastern Indian River and northeastern St. Lucie counties after 2 to 4 inches of rain fell in parts of the area. The advisory warned of minor flooding in low-lying and poorly drained areas. The School District of Indian River County closed all public schools and district offices Thursday, saying saturated ground and expected rain could make travel unsafe for students and staff.

cards.headline: Boil water notice extended 24 hours for 21,000 customers in western Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: A precautionary boil water notice for about 21,000 customers in western Port St. Lucie has been extended by 24 hours as the city continues water-quality testing after a contractor
cards.body:
A precautionary boil water notice for about 21,000 customers in western Port St. Lucie has been extended by 24 hours as the city continues water-quality testing after a contractor struck a major water main. The contractor was working on a non-city construction project when the 36-inch main was hit near Glades Cut Off Road. Crews finished repairs Tuesday evening and began flushing the water system.

 Water service has been fully restored, but the precautionary notice remains in place. Customers must continue boiling water for drinking and other specified uses until the city announces that the notice has been lifted.

 The affected area includes Tradition, Riverland, Western Grove, Wilson Grove, Southern Grove, Copper Creek, Wylder and Verano. Properties along Glades Cut Off Road are also covered by the advisory. City officials said water-quality sampling is underway and laboratory results must confirm that the water is safe to drink before the notice can end.

 Officials also said the number of customers affected means the advisory could continue beyond its initial 48-hour timeframe. The 24-hour extension gives the city more time to complete testing, with the notice still dependent on confirmation that the water is safe.

 For resident Marcus Rowe, a sudden loss of water pressure was the first indication that something was wrong. “I went to turn on the faucet, and the water pressure was low. I was like, 'what's going on'?” he said. Since the disruption, his family has relied on bottled water and boiled water to meet daily needs. Rowe said the family was following the instructions while taking the inconvenience in stride. “Boiling water, doing what they told us to do,” he said. “It's something small, I'm not really sweating it.” His family is continuing those precautions while the advisory remains active.

 Residents covered by the notice are advised to boil water used for drinking, cooking, making ice, brushing their teeth and washing dishes. Those instructions remain in effect despite the restoration of water service and the completion of repairs to the broken main. For households such as the Rowes, that means continuing to use bottled water or boil water for daily needs rather than returning to normal use of tap water.

 The city has said the notice will stay in place until laboratory testing confirms the water is safe to drink. Customers should continue the precautions until the city announces that the advisory has ended.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie police use GTA VI launch to warn against reckless driving
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie Police Department used Thursday’s Grand Theft Auto VI launch to remind fans that reckless driving and other crimes carry consequences beyond a video game. In a l
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie Police Department used Thursday’s Grand Theft Auto VI launch to remind fans that reckless driving and other crimes carry consequences beyond a video game. In a lighthearted safety message, police warned that U.S. 1 and Crosstown are not places to race and that drivers cannot restart after a real-world crash. The department borrowed the game’s wanted-level system to urge residents to avoid attracting police attention.

 Its reminders included obeying red lights, keeping vehicles off sidewalks and leaving patrol cars alone. Police also joked about avoiding an encounter with the SWAT team, encouraging players to keep the game’s lawbreaking on screen.

 Grand Theft Auto VI officially launches Nov. 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Its fictional state, Leonida, is modeled on Florida, with the Miami-inspired Vice City at its center. The story follows Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos as their criminal plans draw them into a statewide conspiracy.

 Florida has also become part of the game’s promotion. In September, a large pink sign welcoming visitors to Vice City appeared on Miami’s Kaseya Center under an agreement between Miami-Dade County and Rockstar Games. County officials expected the arrangement to generate nearly $1 million in revenue and provide marketing opportunities. The Miami Heat held a Vice City-themed celebration Wednesday, with a Thursday launch party planned at the Clevelander South Beach and a Rockstar festival scheduled for Saturday.

 Other police agencies have used the release to distinguish fictional crimes from real offenses. Atlanta police warned against reckless driving, impaired driving, vehicle theft and violence. In South Florida, law enforcement leaders questioned public involvement in promoting the game.

 The Miami-Dade Association of Chiefs of Police opposed marketing the county as Vice City, citing depictions of violence against women and police officers. Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz also questioned whether public agencies should promote a game centered on crimes her department works to stop. Port St. Lucie’s message focused on safe driving and keeping virtual criminal behavior away from local roads.

 The launch could also disrupt work and viewing habits. A GameSquare survey of 1,000 U.S. employees found that 10% of full-time respondents who identified as gamers planned to miss work on launch day, while another 30% were considering time off. Among those considering an absence, 36% said they would report being sick.

 Forty-two percent expected lower productivity. Surveyed gamers anticipated spending about $400 on the game and related purchases and playing a median of 15 hours during the opening weekend. Seventy percent said they might skip sports to play, and 42% expected to be less likely to watch NFL games that weekend. Indian River County students had Thursday off because of forecast weather and flooding concerns, while St. Lucie schools reopened.

hero.headline: Boil water notice extended 24 hours for 21,000 customers in western Port St. Lucie
hero.teaser: A precautionary boil water notice for about 21,000 customers in western Port St. Lucie has been extended by 24 hours as the city continues water-quality testing after a contractor
hero.body:
A precautionary boil water notice for about 21,000 customers in western Port St. Lucie has been extended by 24 hours as the city continues water-quality testing after a contractor struck a major water main. The contractor was working on a non-city construction project when the 36-inch main was hit near Glades Cut Off Road. Crews finished repairs Tuesday evening and began flushing the water system.

 Water service has been fully restored, but the precautionary notice remains in place. Customers must continue boiling water for drinking and other specified uses until the city announces that the notice has been lifted.

 The affected area includes Tradition, Riverland, Western Grove, Wilson Grove, Southern Grove, Copper Creek, Wylder and Verano. Properties along Glades Cut Off Road are also covered by the advisory. City officials said water-quality sampling is underway and laboratory results must confirm that the water is safe to drink before the notice can end.

 Officials also said the number of customers affected means the advisory could continue beyond its initial 48-hour timeframe. The 24-hour extension gives the city more time to complete testing, with the notice still dependent on confirmation that the water is safe.

 For resident Marcus Rowe, a sudden loss of water pressure was the first indication that something was wrong. “I went to turn on the faucet, and the water pressure was low. I was like, 'what's going on'?” he said. Since the disruption, his family has relied on bottled water and boiled water to meet daily needs. Rowe said the family was following the instructions while taking the inconvenience in stride. “Boiling water, doing what they told us to do,” he said. “It's something small, I'm not really sweating it.” His family is continuing those precautions while the advisory remains active.

 Residents covered by the notice are advised to boil water used for drinking, cooking, making ice, brushing their teeth and washing dishes. Those instructions remain in effect despite the restoration of water service and the completion of repairs to the broken main. For households such as the Rowes, that means continuing to use bottled water or boil water for daily needs rather than returning to normal use of tap water.

 The city has said the notice will stay in place until laboratory testing confirms the water is safe to drink. Customers should continue the precautions until the city announces that the advisory has ended.

hero.headline: Indian River County public schools to close Friday as flooding shuts roads
hero.teaser: Public schools across Indian River County will be closed Friday, Nov. 20, after flooding left more roads impassable and raised concerns about additional rain. The School District o
hero.body:
Public schools across Indian River County will be closed Friday, Nov. 20, after flooding left more roads impassable and raised concerns about additional rain. The School District of Indian River County announced the decision Thursday, pointing to localized flooding, already saturated ground and the potential for more heavy rainfall. District officials said the shutdown was intended to protect students, their families and school employees.

 The announcement applies to all of the county’s public schools. It comes as road closures increase, particularly in Vero Lake Estates, and water levels rise at the district’s North County Transportation compound.

 The county’s road closure map showed nine road closures and four lane closures Thursday. Among the roads listed as closed were 100th Court, 103rd Avenue, 104th Avenue, 83rd Street and 87th Street. Those five roads were part of the larger set of closures shown on the map, rather than a complete list of affected roads.

 Vero Lake Estates was a particular concern in both the district’s closure announcement and the Indian River County Sheriff’s Office’s flooding reports. The district cited the growing number of road closures there, while the sheriff’s office reported additional flooded roads in the neighborhood.

 Deputies warned motorists against driving into standing water. Floodwater can be deeper than it looks, and vehicles can stall after entering it, according to the sheriff’s office. That warning accompanied the agency’s reports of more flooded roads in Vero Lake Estates.

 High-water vehicles are in the area, and anyone who becomes stranded should call 911. The safety message applies even when a driver cannot judge the depth of water covering a road: its appearance may not reflect how deep it actually is. The sheriff’s office’s advice was to stay out of the water rather than attempt to drive through it.

 A flood watch remains in effect for Indian River County through Friday evening, with additional showers and thunderstorms possible. The National Weather Service reported that parts of eastern Indian River County had received 2 to 4 inches of rain. The possibility of further rainfall, combined with saturated ground and existing flooding, was among the reasons the district gave for canceling Friday’s classes.

 Beyond the weather-related closure, schools will also be closed for Thanksgiving break. The district’s immediate concern Thursday was the flooding affecting local roads and its North County Transportation compound, with Friday’s shutdown intended to keep students, families and employees safe.

cards.headline: Flooded roads disrupt Indian River County travel; trash service could be affected
cards.teaser: Officials urged drivers to avoid flooded roads in Vero Lake Estates and watch two potential trouble spots in Fellsmere. Unsafe conditions could also disrupt trash collection and close waste facilities early.
cards.body:
The Indian River County Sheriff’s Office reported more flooded roads in Vero Lake Estates on Thursday as heavy rain moved through the county, while county officials warned that unsafe conditions could disrupt trash collection and waste facilities. The sheriff’s office urged drivers to stay off flooded roads because water can be deeper than it appears and can stall vehicles. High-water vehicles are in the area, and anyone who becomes stranded should call 911.

 The county’s road closure map listed nine road closures and four lane closures as of 10:53 a.m. Thursday. Roads marked closed included 100th Court, 103rd Avenue, 104th Avenue, 83rd Street and 87th Street.

 Lane-closure listings included 101st Avenue and West 98th Avenue. In Fellsmere, the city urged drivers to use extreme caution and identified New York Avenue near Hickory Street and North Broadway as potential trouble spots. Those roads could close if rain continues, the city said. City Hall remains open and operating normally.

 The county warned that heavy rain and gusty winds could disrupt trash collection. Residents whose streets are flooded were asked not to put their carts in the water. The landfill and customer convenience centers could close early if conditions become unsafe.

 A flood watch remains in effect for Indian River County through Friday evening, with more showers and thunderstorms possible. The National Weather Service issued a flood advisory Thursday morning for eastern Indian River and northeastern St. Lucie counties after 2 to 4 inches of rain fell in parts of the area. The advisory warned of minor flooding in low-lying and poorly drained areas. The School District of Indian River County closed all public schools and district offices Thursday, saying saturated ground and expected rain could make travel unsafe for students and staff.
